sentences.text: Acheroraptor was initially described as a mid-sized dromaeosaurid.
The lead author suggested it was similar in size to Deinonychus, estimated at 3.3–3.4 meters long and weighing 60–73 kg, or up to 100 kg.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a nearly complete right maxilla with several teeth, showing minor damage and a missing section of the jugal ramus.
A slight chin is present at the apex of the dentary, which is much weaker than that of Velociraptor.
Analysis suggests Acheroraptor had relatively weak jaws adapted for rapid, slashing bites on smaller prey, similar to Velociraptorinae.
Fossils of Acheroraptor were first collected on 28 August 2009 by commercial collectors in the Hell Creek Formation, 45 km southwest of Jordan, Montana.
The discovered remains include a complete right maxilla and an assigned dentary, both housed at the Royal Ontario Museum.
The Royal Ontario Museum purchased the Acheroraptor fossils from a private collector.
Acheroraptor was scientifically described in 2013 by Canadian paleontologists David Evans, Derek Larson, and Philip J. Currie.
The genus Acheroraptor contains only one species, A. temertyorum, which is based on an isolated maxilla with teeth.
Acheroraptor is classified in the class Reptilia.
Acheroraptor is classified in the family Dromaeosauridae.
Acheroraptor belongs to the parent group Velociraptorinae.
Acheroraptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae, a group of theropods found in the Americas, Antarctica, Asia, and Oceania during the Cretaceous.
Phylogenetic analysis recovered Acheroraptor as a member of the clade containing Eudromaeosauria and Microraptorinae, confirming its placement in Dromaeosauridae and possibly Eudromaeosauria.
Two 2020 studies classified Acheroraptor as a basal member of the subfamily Velociraptorinae, extending the known range of this group to North America.
Acheroraptor fossils were first discovered in the Hell Creek Formation, located in modern-day Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, and Wyoming.
Acheroraptor lived in present-day Montana during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous period.
The fossils come from the upper part of the Hell Creek Formation, dating to the latest Maastrichtian stage immediately before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
The Hell Creek Formation environment where Acheroraptor lived was warm, humid, and swampy with maritime to subtropical conditions.
Palynological data indicates the Acheroraptor holotype locality comes from the lower-middle half of the Hell Creek Formation, not the upper half.

Evans, Larson, and Currie (2013) concluded that Acheroraptor was the only dromaeosaurid from the Hell Creek Formation and that teeth previously attributed to Dromaeosaurus and Saurornitholestes actually belonged to it.
The view that Acheroraptor was the only dromaeosaurid in the Hell Creek Formation was disproven in 2015 with the description of the larger Dakotaraptor.
